{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Sir Roger James Elliott''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|FRS}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Thorpe |first=Michael F. |date=2024 |title=Sir Roger James Elliott. 8 December 1928 — 16 April 2018 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=77|pages=145–162 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2024.0015 |doi-access=free }}</ref> (8 December 1928 – 16 April 2018) was a British [[theoretical physics|theoretical]] physicist specialising in the [[magnetic]], [[semiconductor]], and [[optical physics|optical]] properties of [[condensed matter physics|condensed matter]]. He was awarded the [[Maxwell Medal and Prize]], the [[Guthrie Medal and Prize]], and was elected a [[fellow of the Royal Society]]. He was awarded honorary doctorates by the universities of [[University of Paris|Paris]], [[University of Bath|Bath]], and [[University of Essex|Essex]].

== Life ==
Born in [[Chesterfield, Derbyshire|Chesterfield]], Elliott's father was a policeman, who died of [[tuberculosis]] when Elliott was three.<ref name=":0" /> Elliott was brought up by his mother and three unmarried aunts in [[Swanwick, Derbyshire|Swanwick]], Derbyshire.<ref name=":0" /> Elliott obtained a [[DPhil]] in mathematics and theoretical physics from the [[University of Oxford]] in 1952.<ref name=":0" /> He was a [[theoretical physics|theoretical]] physicist specialising in the [[magnetic]], [[semiconductor]], and [[optical physics|optical]] properties of [[condensed matter physics|condensed matter]]. He was a [[research fellow]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 1952–3, then at the [[Atomic Energy Research Establishment]] until 1955, when he was appointed to a lectureship at the [[University of Reading]]. He returned to the [[University of Oxford]] in 1957, where he was the [[Wykeham Professor]] of Physics from 1974 until 1988. He was [[chief executive]] of [[Oxford University Press]] from 1988 to 1993.<ref name="ae">{{cite web |date=2010-04-12 |title=Roger J. Elliott |url=http://www.ae-info.org/ae/User/Elliott_Roger |accessdate=2011-01-30 |publisher=[[Academia Europaea]]}}</ref>

The [[Institute of Physics]] awarded the [[Maxwell Medal and Prize]] jointly to Elliott and [[Kenneth William Harry Stevens]] in 1968, and the [[Guthrie Medal and Prize]] to Elliott in 1990.<ref>{{cite web |title=Maxwell medal recipients |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/bronze-early-career-medals/james-clerk-maxwell-medal-and-prize-recipients |accessdate=2011-01-30 |publisher=[[Institute of Physics]]}}</ref> Elliott was elected a [[fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1976 and knighted in 1987.<ref name="pot">{{cite web |title=Prof Sir Roger Elliott, FRS |url=http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/search/results/16812/Roger%20James+ELLIOTT.aspx |url-access=subscription |accessdate=2011-01-30 |work=[[Debrett's People of Today]] |publisher=Debrett's}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Faraday medal recipients |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold-medals/michael-faraday-medal-and-prize-recipients |accessdate=2011-01-30 |publisher=Institute of Physics}}</ref> He has been awarded honorary doctorates by the universities of [[University of Paris|Paris]] (1983), [[University of Bath|Bath]] (1991), and [[University of Essex|Essex]] (1993).<ref name="pot" /> Elliott died on 16 April 2018 at the age of 89.<ref name="Death">{{cite web |url=https://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/news/2018/04/19/professor-sir-roger-elliott-frs |title=Professor Sir Roger Elliott FRS |work=News |publisher=[[Department of Physics, University of Oxford]] |date=2018-04-18 |accessdate=2018-04-19 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180420011232/https://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/news/2018/04/19/professor-sir-roger-elliott-frs |archive-date=2018-04-20}}</ref>
